- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).  
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-70+ levels), often overshooting by 5–10% before correcting.  
- Shows persistent lag in capturing downward trends; delays in recognizing price drops by 3–7 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to overcorrect upward after minor dips, then underestimate subsequent recovery.  
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are overly pessimistic in high-price environments (e.g., >75) and overly optimistic in low-price environments (<65).  
- Avoids “tail risk” in early periods — underestimates volatility spikes near end of forecast horizon.
